title: Autotune: defaults for batching/caching, quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Nair
description: Implements an automated autotune pipeline that sets sensible defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, introduces quantization profile support for model variants, and ships a unit-economics (uecon) reporting CLI and dashboard hooks. Motivation: customers want predictable per-token cost improvements without manual tuning; we observed 18-35% unit-cost wins in internal canaries by combining batching + prefix caching + target quantization. Work includes schema and config for default policies, an autotune controller that runs short-profile workloads to choose a profile, quant profile artifacts and validation, integration with cost telemetry to compute estimated token cost and latency SLO impact, and a small UX surface in the console/CLI to preview and roll out recommendations. Checklist: [x] defaults for batching/caching implemented [x] quant profiles and validation [x] uecon tooling (CLI + dashboard hooks) [x] unit, integration, and perf tests [x] canary rollout plan.

release_notes: Autotune defaults: new runtime defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching to reduce per-token cost without manual tuning.
Quant profiles: official artifact format and validator for model quantization recommendations.
Unit-econ tooling: new CLI and dashboard hooks to preview estimated token cost and latency tradeoffs before rollout.
Canary: rollout plan included; initial canary shows 18-35% unit-cost reduction on examined workloads.
